verdict.rationale: DeepInfra is an API-first inference cloud. Its OpenAI-compatible endpoint uses API-token auth and needs only base_url, api_key and model changes, so it can be called non-interactively from scripts. It also offers automation-friendly controls: fail_fast returns an immediate HTTP 429, and the flex tier is aimed at asynchronous workloads. However, nothing in the evidence documents CI usage or headless tooling, and the OpenAPI spec probes returned 404. missing for 10: explicit CI/headless automation documentation, an official CLI, a published OpenAPI spec, independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Point your existing OpenAI SDK to `https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai` and your code works without changes.
Set the optional fail_fast parameter to true to get an immediate HTTP 429 instead of waiting.
It’s ideal for non-production or lower-priority tasks such as model evaluations, data enrichment, and asynchronous workloads.
